chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Safwan and Ibn Abi Umayr, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled regarding a man who consummated the marriage with a woman while he was in the state of ihram, before he had exited it. He ruled that he should release her, and his marriage was not considered valid until he exited the ihram. When he exits, he may propose to her; if her family wishes, they may marry her to him, and if they wish, they may not.
Al-Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: The person in ihram does not contract the marriage; if he contracts it, it is not completed.

key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: One in the state of ihram
key_terms.يُحِلَّ: To exit the state of ihram

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marriage consummation while in the state of ihram during Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), cited by Shaykh al-Tusi in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, clarifies the status of *nikah* (marriage contract) during *ihram* as voidable rather than permanently invalid, distinguishing it from the prohibition of sexual intercourse. The ruling establishes that while the contract is not fully effective until the pilgrim exits the sacred state, the woman is not considered a wife during *ihram*, allowing her family to accept or reject the proposal once the pilgrim is free. This reflects the Shia juristic principle that the impediment of *ihram* suspends the full legal effects of marriage without dissolving the bond entirely.
